exposure: Smoking during pregnancy (no smoking, quit in first trimester, continued smoking)
cohort: The study included all women with singleton pregnancies (N = 791,183) in Finland during the years 2006 to 2018, excluding those with previous kidney diseases, gestational hypertension or diabetes, or preeclampsia.
finding: Both quitting and continuing smoking during pregnancy were associated with isolated proteinuria, and both continued smoking and isolated proteinuria were associated with an increased risk for preterm birth.
